passages.text:
PMSBY is an Accident Insurance Scheme offering accidental death and disability cover for death or disability on account of an accident.
It is a one-year cover, renewable from year to year.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); Introduction

passages.text:
Rs. 2 lakh is payable on member’s death due to accident.
Rs. 2 lakh is payable for Total and irrecoverable loss of both eyes or loss of use of both hands or feet or loss of sight of one eye and loss of use of hand or foot.
Rs. 1 lakh is payable for Total and irrecoverable loss of sight of one eye or loss of use of one hand or foot.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); Benefits

passages.text:
Rs. 20/- per annum per member. However the premium may be revised based on annual claims experience.
The premium will be deducted from the account holder’s bank / Post office account through ‘auto debit’ facility in one instalment, as per the option given, at the time of enrolment under the scheme. However, in cases where auto debit takes place after 1st June, the cover shall commence from the date of auto debit of premium by Bank/ Post office.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); Premium

passages.text:
The cover shall be for one-year period stretching from 1st June to 31st May of every year.
Any individual can join by providing consent for auto debit at the time of enrollment.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); Enrolment modality / period

passages.text: Accident means a sudden, unforeseen and involuntary event caused by external, violent and visible means.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); FAQ, accident definition

passages.text:
What benefit will be payable if a person suffers partial disability without irrecoverable loss of sight of one eye or loss of use of one hand or foot? addremove
No benefit will be payable.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); FAQ, partial disability

passages.text:
Is there any provision for reimbursement of hospitalisation expenses following accident resulting in death or disablement? addremove
No.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); FAQ, hospitalisation expenses

passages.text: No. The insured/ nominee shall be eligible for one claim only.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); FAQ, one claim only

passages.text: All individual account holders of participating banks/ Post office in the age group of 18 to 70 years are entitled to join.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); Scope of coverage

passages.text: In case of multiple bank / Post office accounts held by an individual in one or different banks/ Post office, the person is eligible to join the scheme through one bank/ Post office account only.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); Scope of coverage

passages.text: Individual bank/ Post office account holders of the participating banks/ Post office aged between 18 and 70 years who give their consent to join / enable auto-debit, as per the above modality, will be enrolled into the scheme.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); Eligibility Conditions

passages.text: In case of a joint account, all holders of the said account can join the scheme provided they satisfy its eligibility criteria and pay the premium at the rate of Rs.20 per person per annum through auto-debit.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); FAQ, joint accounts

passages.text: All bank account holders other than institutional account holders are eligible for subscribing to PMSBY scheme.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); FAQ, account types

passages.text: Any NRI having an eligible bank account with a bank branch located in India is eligible for purchase of PMSBY cover subject to fulfillment of the terms and conditions relating to the scheme. However, in case a claim arises, the claim benefit will be paid to the beneficiary/ nominee only in Indian currency.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); FAQ, NRIs

passages.text: Natural calamities being in the nature of accidents, any death / disability (as defined under PMSBY) resulting from such natural calamities is also covered under PMSBY. While death due to suicide is not covered, that from murder is covered.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); FAQ, natural calamities, suicide and murder

passages.text:
The accident cover of the member shall terminate / be restricted accordingly on any of the following events:
On attaining 70 years or the end of the policy tenure of the subscriber already enrolled in the scheme.
Closure of account with the Bank or insufficiency of balance to keep the insurance in force.
In case a member is covered through more than one account and premium is received by the insurance company inadvertently, insurance cover will be restricted to one account and the premium shall be liable to be forfeited.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); FAQ, when can the accident cover assurance terminate

passages.text: The cover shall be for one-year period stretching from 1st June to 31st May. At the time of enrolment, subscriber has to provide consent, to join / pay by auto-debit from the designated individual bank / Post office account, until further instructions, an amount of Rs.20/- (Rupees Twenty only) per annum, or any amount as decided from time to time, which may be intimated immediately if and when revised, towards renewal of coverage under the scheme. Delayed enrolment / renewal subsequent to this date will be possible on payment of annual premium.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); FAQ, enrolment period and modality

passages.text: Yes, new eligible entrants can also join in future years on payment of premium through auto-debit. However, risk cover would start from the date of auto debit of premium from the subscriber’s account.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); FAQ, new entrants in later years

passages.text: Individuals who exit the scheme at any point may re-join the scheme in future years by paying the annual premium, subject to conditions that may be laid down. However, risk cover would start from the date of auto debit of premium from the subscriber’s account.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); FAQ, re-joining

passages.text: In case of death of the account holder/subscriber who enrolled in the scheme, claim can be filed by the nominee/appointee as per the enrolment form or by the legal heir/s in case nominee is pre-deceased.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); FAQ, who can claim

passages.text: Disability claim will be credited in the bank account of the insured bank account holder / subscriber. Death claim will be remitted to the bank account of the nominee / legal heir(s).

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); FAQ, mode of payment of the claim amount

passages.text: In case of incidents like road, rail and similar vehicular accidents, drowning, death involving any crime etc, the accident should be reported to police. In case of incidents like snake bite, fall from tree etc, the cause should be supported by immediate hospital record.

source.locator: JanSuraksha PMSBY page (saved HTML); FAQ, reporting accidents to police

passages.text: Step 01: In order to enrol in PMSBY offline, one can visit the bank branch where one has a savings account or the candidate can visit the official site: https://jansuraksha.gov.in/Forms-PMSBY.aspx to download the form.

source.locator: myScheme page; Application Process, Offline, step 1

passages.text: Step 02: After downloading the application form , candidate can fill in all the details and submit  them to the bank along with the  required documents.

source.locator: myScheme page; Application Process, Offline, step 2

passages.text: Step 03: Once it is successfully submitted , subscriber will get an Acknowledgement Slip Cum Certificate of Insurance.

source.locator: myScheme page; Application Process, Offline, step 3
